items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I knew he was working with Chris Powell, Chris Powell and the Blue Flames... So I saw he was working in the park down in Harlem, so I went down there to see him... We played, you know, “Confirmation,” two or three tunes.

ctx.x: In the past, you’ve stated, as everyone has, the most laudatory things about Clifford Brown. Had you known him before that session?

No, not really. I was working with Elmo. Elmo worked in Dud Bascomb’s band, and I saw him every night—you know, when he showed up. I had heard about Clifford Brown. In fact, all the musicians knew about him. But, like, you know, Max and Art, they wasn’t going to bring him to New York, because they’re looking out for theirself, which is I guess...it’s what you do when you’re a junkie. You live from day to day, trying to cop. So it’s a disastrous situation, but that’s the way it is. I knew he was working with Chris…
Then the following year, the Live at Birdland date with Art Blakey. Had you been playing with Art Blakey for a while?
